title: Evaluation of the acceptance and effectiveness of a new COGITO app self-help module for eating disorders in a randomized controlled trial
summary:
Eating disorders are associated with severe health impairments, affecting both the physical and psychological well-being of those affected. Two of the most common eating disorders are bulimia nervosa and binge-eating disorder. Both conditions manifest symptoms on the following levels: Behavior (e.g., consumption or avoidance of food), cognition (e.g., excessive preoccupation with food and body image), and emotion (e.g., maladaptive emotional regulation through eating and exercise behaviors). The COGITO self-help smartphone app addresses all three levels. Through targeted self-help exercises, the app provides impulses for behavioral change, encourages users to question maladaptive cognitive patterns, and offers functional strategies for emotional regulation.
Early intervention and continuous treatment are crucial for improving the prognosis of eating disorders. However, the time between symptom onset and the start of appropriate treatment is often very long for many individuals. Contributing factors include structural healthcare challenges (e.g., lack of available therapy slots) and individual barriers (e.g., feelings of shame). In both cases, self-help apps can serve as a valuable complement to traditional care. The COGITO app includes a dedicated module on eating disorders, featuring exercises designed to provide psychoeducational information and enhance the well-being of those affected. This module is intentionally designed for individuals with either of the mentioned diagnoses, as well as for those who do not meet the full criteria for an eating disorder but still experience subjective difficulties with eating or body weight.

interventions.name: The first arm of the study consists of the intervention group, which includes participants who self-report currently experiencing bulimia nervosa, binge-eating disorder or subjective problems with eating (see: Investigated Disease/Health Condition). The intervention group will have access to the COG

Waitlist control group (WKG), which will receive access to the app only after completing the post-assessment (T1). Ongoing outpatient treatments initiated before study participation may continue as usual (treatment-as-usual, TAU).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Current symptoms of bulimia nervosa, binge eating disorder or subjective problems with eating according to self-disclosure; sufficient knowledge of German; agreement to the participation criteria; informed consent; availability of internet access and smartphone; willingness to participate in three online surveys; willingness to use the self-help smartphone app for 6 weeks; willingness to leave an anonymized email address for the survey.
Exclusion criteria:
Acute suicidality (measured with the PHQ-9 item 9, cut-off > 2); bipolar disorder; psychotic disorder; current stay in inpatient treatment, BMI <18 kg/m2
